properties.name: Nir Davidson
properties.short_bio: Prof. Nir Davidson is an experimental physicist in the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads a cold-atom and laser-physics laboratory. His research spans the dynamics and precision spectroscopy of ultracold atoms, quantum-degenerate Bose and Fermi gases, atom interferometry, coupled-laser networks, and slow and stored light in hot atomic vapor.

properties.name: Ofer Firstenberg
properties.short_bio: Prof. Ofer Firstenberg is an experimental physicist in the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads the **Light-vs-Matter Lab**. His research asks whether individual photons can be made to behave like massive particles — and atoms like light — through strong, controllable photon-photon interactions. The group works on photon-photon interaction in cold Rydberg gases (photonic molecules and crystals), hot quantum memories spanning nanoseconds to hours, and atom interferometry.

properties.name: Tom Manovitz
properties.short_bio: Dr. Tom Manovitz is an experimental physicist who joined the Department of Physics of Complex Systems at the Weizmann Institute of Science in October 2025, where he leads a new laboratory using high-resolution laser arrays to trap and manipulate individual neutral atoms as a platform for building and probing large, highly entangled quantum systems. His group focuses on entanglement and quantum many-body physics, hardware for neutral-atom quantum processors, and quantum computation and error correction.

properties.name: Serge Rosenblum
properties.short_bio: Dr. Serge Rosenblum is an experimental physicist at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where his group builds superconducting quantum circuits for quantum information processing. His research centers on circuit QED and error-correctable **bosonic qubits** encoded in long-lived superconducting microwave cavities, aiming at hardware-efficient quantum error correction.

properties.name: Daniel Zajfman

current_position.title: Professor of Physics (Particle Physics and Astrophysics)

properties.short_bio: Prof. Daniel Zajfman is an experimental physicist in the Department of Particle Physics and Astrophysics at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where his group ("Molecular Physics and Ion Trapping," with Dr. Oded Heber) studies the dynamics of single atomic, molecular, and cluster ions. He is a pioneer of the **electrostatic ion beam trap** — a linear "electrostatic bottle" that stores fast ion beams between facing electrostatic mirrors without magnetic fields — and uses such traps and storage rings to recreate the extreme conditions of interstellar space in the laboratory, probing dissociative recombination, internal decay processes, and the surprising self-bunching of trapped ions.

properties.name: Barak Dayan
properties.short_bio: Prof. Barak Dayan is an experimental physicist in the Department of Chemical and Biological Physics at the Weizmann Institute of Science, where he leads the **Quantum Optics group**. His research centers on achieving deterministic photon-photon interactions at the single-photon level — using laser-cooled atoms coupled to optical microresonators to let a single atom, or even a single photon, control another photon. His group demonstrated a single-atom all-optical switch and a passive photon-atom quantum gate, foundational primitives for photonic quantum information.

properties.name: John Preskill

current_position.title: Richard P. Feynman Professor of Theoretical Physics; Director, Institute for Quantum Information and Matter (IQIM)

properties.short_bio: John Preskill is a theoretical physicist at Caltech and director of the Institute for Quantum Information and Matter. He coined the term "quantum supremacy" and the NISQ (Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum) era, and is a leading voice on quantum error correction, fault tolerance, and the theory of quantum information.

properties.name: Ignacio Cirac

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics
current_position.title: Director, Theory Division

properties.short_bio: J. Ignacio Cirac is a theoretical physicist and director of the Theory Division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics. With Peter Zoller he proposed the 1995 Cirac-Zoller scheme for a trapped-ion quantum gate -- the blueprint for much of trapped-ion quantum computing -- and has made foundational contributions to quantum simulation and tensor-network methods.

properties.name: Serge Haroche
properties.short_bio: Serge Haroche is a French physicist who shared the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics with David Wineland for ground-breaking experimental methods that enable measuring and manipulating individual quantum systems. At the Ecole Normale Superieure and College de France he pioneered cavity quantum electrodynamics, trapping single photons and probing them non-destructively with Rydberg atoms.

properties.name: Alain Aspect
properties.short_bio: Alain Aspect shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments with entangled photons that established the violation of Bell inequalities and pioneered quantum information science. A professor at the Institut d'Optique, he is also a co-founder of the neutral-atom quantum-computing company Pasqal.

properties.name: Carl Wieman

current_position.title: Professor of Physics and of Education (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

properties.short_bio: Carl Wieman shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics with Eric Cornell and Wolfgang Ketterle for creating the first Bose-Einstein condensate in a dilute gas of rubidium atoms (1995) at JILA. He is now a professor at Stanford, also renowned for his work on science education.

properties.name: Eric A. Cornell

current_position.institution: University of Colorado Boulder / JILA / NIST
current_position.title: Professor of Physics; NIST Fellow (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

properties.short_bio: Eric Cornell shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics for producing, with Carl Wieman, the first gaseous Bose-Einstein condensate at JILA in 1995. A NIST and University of Colorado physicist, he continues to lead precision-measurement and ultracold-atom research.

properties.name: Wolfgang Ketterle

current_position.title: John D. MacArthur Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2001)

properties.short_bio: Wolfgang Ketterle shared the 2001 Nobel Prize in Physics for achieving Bose-Einstein condensation in dilute atomic gases and for early fundamental studies of the condensates' properties. At MIT he leads research on ultracold atoms and quantum simulation of many-body physics.

properties.name: William D. Phillips

current_position.title: NIST Fellow & Distinguished University Professor (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1997)

properties.short_bio: William D. Phillips shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics with Steven Chu and Claude Cohen-Tannoudji for developing methods to cool and trap atoms with laser light. A NIST Fellow and co-founder of the Joint Quantum Institute, he works on ultracold atoms, atom optics, and quantum simulation.

properties.name: Steven Chu

current_position.title: William R. Kenan Jr. Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1997)

properties.short_bio: Steven Chu shared the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics for the laser cooling and trapping of atoms. A professor at Stanford, he later served as the 12th U.S. Secretary of Energy (2009-2013) and mentored a generation of atomic physicists, including Nir Davidson.

properties.name: Theodor W. Hansch

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics / LMU Munich
current_position.title: Director; Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2005)

properties.short_bio: Theodor W. Hansch shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics for contributions to laser-based precision spectroscopy, including the optical frequency-comb technique. He directs a division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and is a professor at LMU Munich.

properties.name: Jean Dalibard

current_position.institution: College de France / Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, ENS
current_position.title: Professor

properties.short_bio: Jean Dalibard is a French physicist at the College de France and Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, known for foundational work on laser cooling (Sisyphus cooling, the magneto-optical trap), quantum gases, and synthetic gauge fields in ultracold atoms.

properties.name: Gerhard Rempe

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics
current_position.title: Director, Quantum Dynamics Division

properties.short_bio: Gerhard Rempe directs the Quantum Dynamics Division at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics. His group pioneered cavity quantum electrodynamics with single atoms, deterministic atom-photon entanglement, and elementary quantum networks and quantum logic with light.

properties.name: H. Jeff Kimble

current_position.title: William L. Valentine Professor and Professor of Physics, Emeritus

properties.short_bio: H. Jeff Kimble is a pioneer of experimental quantum optics and cavity QED at Caltech. His group demonstrated landmark results in photon antibunching, quantum teleportation of light, and the concept of the "quantum internet" built from atom-photon interfaces.

properties.name: Anton Zeilinger
properties.short_bio: Anton Zeilinger shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics for experiments with entangled photons establishing Bell-inequality violations and pioneering quantum information science. Based at the University of Vienna, he demonstrated quantum teleportation and long-distance entanglement distribution.

properties.name: Jean-Michel Raimond
properties.short_bio: Jean-Michel Raimond is a French physicist at Sorbonne Universite and the Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, where, with Serge Haroche, he developed cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments probing the quantum-to-classical transition with Rydberg atoms and microwave photons.

properties.name: Philippe Grangier

current_position.institution: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique / CNRS
current_position.title: Research Director (CNRS)

properties.short_bio: Philippe Grangier is a CNRS physicist at the Institut d'Optique whose early experiments demonstrated single-photon behaviour and wave-particle duality. His group pioneered single-atom trapping in optical tweezers and Rydberg-atom quantum gates, foundational to neutral-atom quantum computing.

properties.name: John L. Hall

current_position.institution: JILA / NIST / University of Colorado Boulder
current_position.title: Senior Scientist Emeritus (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 2005)

properties.short_bio: John L. 'Jan' Hall shared the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physics for contributions to laser-based precision spectroscopy and the optical frequency-comb technique. A long-time JILA/NIST scientist, his work underpins modern optical atomic clocks and precision measurement.

properties.name: Marlan O. Scully
properties.short_bio: Marlan O. Scully is a theoretical physicist at Texas A&M (and affiliated with Princeton and Baylor) known for foundational work in quantum optics, including the laser phase-transition analogy, lasing without inversion, the micromaser, and quantum coherence effects. He co-authored the standard text Quantum Optics.

properties.name: Hans Dehmelt

current_position.title: Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1989)

properties.short_bio: Hans Georg Dehmelt (1922–2017) was a German-American physicist who shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing the ion-trap (Penning-trap) technique. After a doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Hans Kopfermann and postdoctoral work at Duke University with Walter Gordy, he joined the University of Washington, where his group isolated and observed a single trapped barium ion and a single electron confined as "geonium," enabling the most precise measurement of the electron magnetic moment (g-factor) and founding the field of single-particle precision spectroscopy that underlies modern trapped-ion quantum computing.

properties.name: Norman F. Ramsey

current_position.title: Higgins Professor of Physics (Nobel Laureate in Physics, 1989)

properties.short_bio: Norman F. Ramsey shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physics for the separated oscillatory fields method (Ramsey interferometry) and the invention of the hydrogen maser. His techniques are the basis of atomic clocks and precision spectroscopy. A Harvard professor, he died in 2011.

properties.name: Dorit Aharonov
properties.short_bio: Dorit Aharonov is a theoretical computer scientist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem renowned for the quantum threshold theorem (fault-tolerant quantum computation), adiabatic quantum computing, and quantum complexity. She is a co-founder and chief scientific officer of the quantum-error-mitigation company Qedma.

properties.name: Netanel Lindner
properties.short_bio: Netanel Lindner is a theoretical condensed-matter and quantum-information physicist at the Technion, known for work on topological phases, Floquet engineering, and quantum error characterization. He is a co-founder and CTO of the quantum-error-mitigation company Qedma.

properties.name: Shay Hacohen-Gourgy
properties.short_bio: Shay Hacohen-Gourgy is an experimental physicist at the Technion specializing in superconducting quantum circuits, quantum measurement, and feedback control. He is a co-founder and CTO of QuamCore, a startup developing a scalable superconducting quantum processor.

properties.name: Yoav Sagi
properties.short_bio: Yoav Sagi is an experimental physicist at the Technion leading an ultracold-atoms laboratory focused on quantum-degenerate Fermi gases and many-body physics. He is a co-founder of the neutral-atom quantum-computing startup Q-Factor.

properties.name: A. Paul Alivisatos

current_position.title: President of the University of Chicago; Professor of Chemistry

properties.short_bio: A. Paul Alivisatos is a chemist and president of the University of Chicago, internationally known for pioneering work on semiconductor nanocrystals (quantum dots) and their applications.

properties.name: Aharon Kapitulnik

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

properties.short_bio: Aharon Kapitulnik is a condensed-matter physicist at Stanford studying superconductivity, quantum materials and high-precision measurement.

properties.name: Alex Kuzmich
properties.short_bio: Alex Kuzmich is an experimental physicist known for pioneering work on quantum memories and entanglement in atomic ensembles for quantum networking.

properties.name: Alex Retzker
properties.short_bio: Alex Retzker is a theoretical physicist at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem working on quantum information, quantum sensing with NV centers and trapped ions, and quantum control.

properties.name: Alexander Gaeta

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Materials Science

properties.short_bio: Alexander Gaeta is an experimental physicist at Columbia known for nonlinear and quantum nanophotonics, including chip-scale frequency combs and quantum light sources.

properties.name: Alexander Pines
properties.short_bio: Alexander Pines is a chemist at UC Berkeley renowned for foundational advances in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and magnetic resonance imaging.

properties.name: Alexander Sergienko

current_position.title: Professor of Electrical & Computer Engineering and of Physics

properties.short_bio: Alexander Sergienko is an experimental physicist at Boston University working on quantum optics, entangled-photon sources, and quantum communication.

properties.name: Anatole Abragam
properties.short_bio: Anatole Abragam was a French physicist and a founding figure of nuclear magnetic resonance, author of the classic text The Principles of Nuclear Magnetism. He died in 2011.

properties.name: Andrew Steane
properties.short_bio: Andrew M. Steane is a Professor of Physics at the University of Oxford and a fellow of Exeter College. He co-discovered quantum error correction — the CSS/"Steane" codes — and initiated Oxford's trapped-ion quantum-computing experiments, which he later co-led with David Lucas using calcium-ion (⁴⁰Ca⁺ and ⁴³Ca⁺) qubits. He received the Institute of Physics Maxwell Medal and Prize in 2000 and has written several physics textbooks. His work spans both the theory and experimental implementation of quantum information with trapped ions.

properties.name: Andrew White
properties.short_bio: Andrew White is an experimental physicist at the University of Queensland and a pioneer of photonic quantum information science and quantum process tomography.

properties.name: Atac Imamoglu
properties.short_bio: Atac Imamoglu is a physicist at ETH Zurich known for semiconductor quantum optics, quantum dots as single-photon sources and spin qubits, and exciton-polariton physics.

properties.name: Beat H. Meier
properties.short_bio: Beat H. Meier is a physical chemist at ETH Zurich recognized for advances in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

properties.name: Brian Pippard
properties.short_bio: Sir Brian Pippard was a British physicist at Cambridge, a leading figure in superconductivity and the electronic structure of metals, and a founder of Cambridge's Cavendish reforms. He died in 2008.

properties.name: Carl Williams

current_position.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
current_position.title: Physicist; former Deputy Director, Physical Measurement Laboratory

properties.short_bio: Carl J. Williams is a physicist at NIST who has worked on ultracold-atom theory and has been a long-standing leader of U.S. quantum-information science programs.

properties.name: Charles Clark
properties.short_bio: Charles W. Clark is a theoretical AMO physicist and a Fellow of the Joint Quantum Institute, with research spanning atom optics, neutron interferometry and quantum information.

properties.name: Charles M. Marcus

current_position.institution: Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen / University of Washington
current_position.title: Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Charles Marcus is an experimental physicist known for mesoscopic physics, semiconductor spin qubits and topological (Majorana) quantum-computing research.

properties.name: Cindy A. Regal
properties.short_bio: Cindy Regal is an experimental physicist at JILA working on optomechanics and single neutral atoms in optical tweezers for quantum information.

properties.name: Colin Webb
properties.short_bio: Colin Webb is a laser physicist at Oxford known for the development of gas and excimer lasers and a co-founder of Oxford Lasers.

properties.name: Constantin Piron
properties.short_bio: Constantin Piron was a Swiss theoretical physicist known for foundational work on quantum logic and the axiomatic structure of quantum mechanics. He died in 2019.

properties.name: Duncan G. Steel

current_position.title: Robert J. Hiller Professor of Engineering; Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Duncan G. Steel is an experimental physicist at the University of Michigan working on coherent optical control of semiconductor quantum dots and spins.

properties.name: Dan Rugar
properties.short_bio: Dan Rugar is a physicist at IBM Almaden who pioneered magnetic resonance force microscopy, achieving single-electron-spin detection, and nanomechanical sensing.

properties.name: Dan Walls
properties.short_bio: Daniel F. Walls was a New Zealand theoretical physicist and a founder of modern quantum optics theory, including squeezed states; co-author of the text Quantum Optics. He died in 1999.

properties.name: Dana Anderson
properties.short_bio: Dana Anderson is an experimental physicist at JILA working on atom optics and compact cold-atom systems, and a founder of ColdQuanta (now Infleqtion).

properties.name: Daniel Prober

current_position.title: Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

properties.short_bio: Daniel Prober is an experimental physicist at Yale known for superconducting and nanoscale detectors, including hot-electron bolometers and single-photon sensors.

properties.name: David DeMille
properties.short_bio: David DeMille is an experimental physicist known for precision molecular measurements (the ACME electron-EDM experiment) and proposals for polar-molecule quantum computing.

properties.name: David Hall
properties.short_bio: David Hall is an experimental physicist at Amherst College working on Bose-Einstein condensates and topological excitations such as quantum knots and monopoles.

properties.name: David Kielpinski
properties.short_bio: David Kielpinski is a physicist known for the influential QCCD (quantum charge-coupled device) architecture for scalable trapped-ion quantum computers, developed in the NIST Ion Storage Group of David J. Wineland using ⁹Be⁺ ions (Kielpinski, Monroe & Wineland, *Nature* 2002). He later led trapped-ion and quantum-optics research at the Centre for Quantum Dynamics, Griffith University, in Brisbane, Australia.

properties.name: Deborah Jin

current_position.institution: JILA / NIST / University of Colorado Boulder
current_position.title: Fellow, JILA/NIST (1968-2016)

properties.short_bio: Deborah Jin was an experimental physicist at JILA who created the first fermionic condensate and pioneered ultracold polar molecules and degenerate Fermi gases. She died in 2016.

properties.name: Edvardas Narevicius

current_position.title: Professor of Chemical and Biological Physics

properties.short_bio: Edvardas Narevicius is an experimental physicist at the Weizmann Institute known for merged-beam techniques to study chemical reactions at very low temperatures (cold chemistry).

properties.name: Evelyn Hu

current_position.title: Tarr-Coyne Professor of Applied Physics and of Electrical Engineering

properties.short_bio: Evelyn Hu is an applied physicist at Harvard working on nanophotonics and quantum materials, including color centers and quantum-dot devices.

properties.name: Francesco De Martini
properties.short_bio: Francesco De Martini is an Italian experimental physicist and a pioneer of quantum optics, including quantum cloning and entangled-photon experiments.

properties.name: Franco N. C. Wong

current_position.title: Senior Research Scientist, Research Laboratory of Electronics

properties.short_bio: Franco Wong is a research scientist at MIT working on entangled-photon sources and quantum communication.

properties.name: Frederic Merkt
properties.short_bio: Frederic Merkt is a physical chemist at ETH Zurich known for high-resolution molecular spectroscopy and the study of Rydberg states and cold molecules.

properties.name: Gerard Milburn
properties.short_bio: Gerard Milburn is a theoretical physicist at the University of Queensland known for foundational work in quantum optics, quantum measurement and quantum information; co-author of Quantum Optics.

properties.name: Gerd Schon
properties.short_bio: Gerd Schon is a theoretical physicist at KIT known for the theory of superconducting qubits and quantum transport in nanostructures.

properties.name: Gianni Blatter
properties.short_bio: Gianni Blatter is a theoretical physicist at ETH Zurich known for the theory of vortices in superconductors and proposals for solid-state and superconducting qubits.

properties.name: Gunter Werth
properties.short_bio: Günter Werth is a German experimental physicist, Professor (emeritus) at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, known for high-precision measurements with Penning and Paul ion traps. After a doctorate at the University of Bonn (1969) he joined Mainz, led the ISOLTRAP experiment at CERN, and later headed the Cooled and Stored Ions division at the Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics in Heidelberg. His work includes precise determinations of atomic and ion g-factors and masses — using species ranging from calcium ions to highly charged ions — and tests of fundamental symmetries.

properties.name: Guo Guangcan

current_position.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
current_position.title: Professor of Physics; CAS Academician

properties.short_bio: Guo Guangcan is a physicist at USTC and a founder of quantum information research in China, working on quantum optics and quantum communication.

properties.name: Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop
properties.short_bio: Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop is an experimental physicist at the University of Queensland known for optical tweezers, laser micromanipulation and atom optics.

properties.name: Harry Buhrman
properties.short_bio: Harry Buhrman is a theoretical computer scientist and director of QuSoft, known for quantum complexity theory and quantum communication complexity.

properties.name: Herbert Walther

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics / LMU Munich
current_position.title: Director (1935-2006)

properties.short_bio: Herbert Walther was a German physicist and long-time director at the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, a pioneer of cavity QED, the one-atom maser and single-ion experiments. He died in 2006.

properties.name: Jacqueline Bloch

current_position.institution: Centre de Nanosciences et de Nanotechnologies (C2N), CNRS / Universite Paris-Saclay
current_position.title: Research Director (CNRS)

properties.short_bio: Jacqueline Bloch is a French physicist known for experiments on exciton-polaritons in semiconductor microcavities and their use for quantum simulation of light.

properties.name: Jan-Michael Rost

current_position.institution: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems
current_position.title: Director, Finite Systems Division

properties.short_bio: Jan-Michael Rost is a theoretical physicist and director at the MPI for the Physics of Complex Systems, working on ultracold Rydberg systems and ultrafast atomic dynamics.

properties.name: Jay Gupta
properties.short_bio: Jay Gupta is an experimental physicist at Ohio State using scanning tunneling microscopy to build and probe atomic-scale structures and spins.

properties.name: Jelena Vuckovic

current_position.title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Applied Physics

properties.short_bio: Jelena Vuckovic is an engineer-physicist at Stanford and a leader in quantum nanophotonics, photonic crystal cavities and color-center quantum devices.

properties.name: Jelmer Renema
properties.short_bio: Jelmer Renema is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on photonic quantum computing and the theory of boson sampling.

properties.name: John M. Doyle

current_position.title: Henry B. Silsbee Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: John Doyle is an experimental physicist at Harvard and a leader in the cooling and trapping of cold and ultracold molecules for precision measurement and quantum science.

properties.name: Jorg Schmiedmayer
properties.short_bio: Jorg Schmiedmayer is an experimental physicist at TU Wien known for atom chips, matter-wave interferometry and quantum simulation of many-body dynamics with ultracold atoms.

properties.name: Jose Ignacio Latorre

current_position.institution: University of Barcelona / Technology Innovation Institute
current_position.title: Professor of Theoretical Physics

properties.short_bio: Jose Ignacio Latorre is a theoretical physicist working on quantum information, tensor networks and quantum machine learning, and has led quantum-technology institutes in Singapore and Abu Dhabi.

properties.name: Josh Nunn
properties.short_bio: Josh Nunn is a physicist at the University of Bath working on photonic quantum memories and quantum light-matter interfaces.

properties.name: Juan Pablo Paz
properties.short_bio: Juan Pablo Paz is a theoretical physicist at the University of Buenos Aires known for work on decoherence, quantum information and the quantum-to-classical transition.

properties.name: K. Birgitta Whaley

current_position.title: Professor of Chemistry; Director, Berkeley Quantum Information & Computation Center

properties.short_bio: K. Birgitta Whaley is a theoretical chemist at UC Berkeley working on quantum information, quantum control and quantum effects in biological systems.

properties.name: Keith Burnett
properties.short_bio: Keith Burnett is a theoretical AMO physicist known for work on ultracold atoms and Bose-Einstein condensates; he later served as a university vice-chancellor.

properties.name: Klaus Boller
properties.short_bio: Klaus Boller is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on laser physics, nonlinear and integrated optics.

properties.name: Kyungwon An
properties.short_bio: Kyungwon An is an experimental physicist at Seoul National University known for cavity quantum electrodynamics and the single-atom laser (microlaser).

properties.name: Lu Jeu Sham
properties.short_bio: Lu Jeu Sham is a condensed-matter theorist at UC San Diego, co-developer of the Kohn-Sham density functional theory and a contributor to semiconductor spin-coherence and spintronics.

properties.name: Leo Kouwenhoven
properties.short_bio: Leo Kouwenhoven is an experimental physicist at TU Delft known for semiconductor quantum dots and experiments on Majorana zero modes for topological quantum computing.

properties.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
properties.short_bio: Lieven Vandersypen is an experimental physicist at TU Delft/QuTech and a leader in semiconductor spin qubits; he earlier helped demonstrate Shor's algorithm with NMR.

properties.name: Markus Oberthaler
properties.short_bio: Markus Oberthaler is an experimental physicist at Heidelberg working on atom interferometry, spin-squeezing and quantum simulation with Bose-Einstein condensates.

properties.name: Martin Plenio

current_position.title: Professor of Theoretical Physics; Director, Institute of Theoretical Physics

properties.short_bio: Martin Plenio is a theoretical physicist at Ulm known for foundational work on entanglement theory, quantum information and quantum effects in biology and NV-diamond sensing.

properties.name: Matthias Weidemuller
properties.short_bio: Matthias Weidemuller is an experimental physicist at Heidelberg working on ultracold atoms and molecules and Rydberg-atom quantum simulation.

properties.name: Michael G. Raymer
properties.short_bio: Michael Raymer is an experimental physicist at the University of Oregon known for quantum optics and a leading advocate for the U.S. National Quantum Initiative.

properties.name: Michael S. Chapman
properties.short_bio: Michael Chapman is an experimental physicist at Georgia Tech working on Bose-Einstein condensates, spinor gases and atom-cavity quantum optics.

properties.name: Michel Orrit
properties.short_bio: Michel Orrit is an experimental physicist at Leiden University and a pioneer of single-molecule optical detection and spectroscopy.

properties.name: Mikko Mottonen
properties.short_bio: Mikko Mottonen is an experimental physicist at Aalto University working on superconducting qubits and quantum thermodynamics, and a co-founder of IQM Quantum Computers.

properties.name: Neil B. Manson
properties.short_bio: Neil Manson is an experimental physicist at the ANU and a pioneer of the optical and spin physics of the nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond.

properties.name: Niek van Hulst

current_position.institution: ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences
current_position.title: ICREA Professor

properties.short_bio: Niek van Hulst is an experimental physicist at ICFO working on nano-optics, single-molecule and single-emitter photonics and ultrafast nanoscopy.

properties.name: Paolo Villoresi
properties.short_bio: Paolo Villoresi is an experimental physicist at the University of Padua known for quantum communication over long distances and satellite quantum key distribution.

properties.name: Paul L. McEuen

current_position.title: John A. Newman Professor of Physical Science

properties.short_bio: Paul McEuen is an experimental physicist at Cornell known for nanoscience, carbon-nanotube and graphene devices, and atomic-scale machines.

properties.name: Paul Vitanyi
properties.short_bio: Paul Vitanyi is a theoretical computer scientist at CWI known for Kolmogorov complexity and contributions to the theory of quantum computation.

properties.name: Pepijn Pinkse
properties.short_bio: Pepijn Pinkse is an experimental physicist at the University of Twente working on quantum optics, complex photonic media and physical-layer security.

properties.name: Peter Lambropoulos
properties.short_bio: Peter Lambropoulos is a theoretical AMO physicist known for multiphoton and strong-field atomic processes and quantum optics.

properties.name: Peter Leek
properties.short_bio: Peter Leek is an experimental physicist at Oxford developing superconducting qubits and the coaxial-circuit (3D-integrated) approach to scalable processors.

properties.name: Peter Mosley
properties.short_bio: Peter Mosley is an experimental physicist at the University of Bath working on fibre-based single-photon sources and integrated quantum photonics.

properties.name: Peter Schmelcher
properties.short_bio: Peter Schmelcher is a theoretical physicist at the University of Hamburg working on quantum dynamics of complex atomic and molecular systems and ultracold few-body physics.

properties.name: Pierre Rouchon
properties.short_bio: Pierre Rouchon is a control theorist at Mines Paris known for quantum control and feedback stabilization, including work underpinning cavity-QED and cat-qubit experiments.

properties.name: Randy Hulet

current_position.title: Fayez Sarofim Professor of Physics & Astronomy

properties.short_bio: Randy Hulet is an experimental physicist at Rice University known for early Bose-Einstein condensation with attractive interactions and ultracold-atom quantum simulation.

properties.name: Richard N. Zare

current_position.title: Marguerite Blake Wilbur Professor in Natural Science

properties.short_bio: Richard Zare is a chemist at Stanford renowned for laser studies of chemical reactions and the development of laser-induced fluorescence.

properties.name: Robert A. Buhrman

current_position.title: J. E. Sweet Professor of Engineering, Emeritus

properties.short_bio: Robert Buhrman is an applied physicist at Cornell known for nanoscale magnetism and spintronics, including spin-torque devices for memory.

properties.name: Robert M. Westervelt

current_position.title: Mallinckrodt Professor of Applied Physics and of Physics

properties.short_bio: Robert Westervelt is an experimental physicist at Harvard working on nanoscale and mesoscopic electronic systems and scanned-probe imaging.

properties.name: Roberta Ramponi
properties.short_bio: Roberta Ramponi is an experimental physicist at Politecnico di Milano known for integrated and laser-written photonics for quantum applications.

properties.name: Rodolfo Miranda

current_position.institution: Autonomous University of Madrid / IMDEA Nanoscience
current_position.title: Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Rodolfo Miranda is an experimental physicist in Madrid known for surface science, nanomagnetism and scanning-probe studies of low-dimensional materials.

properties.name: Ronald L. Walsworth
properties.short_bio: Ronald Walsworth is an experimental physicist at the University of Maryland and a leader in NV-diamond quantum sensing and precision measurement.

properties.name: Shinji Urabe
properties.short_bio: Shinji Urabe is an experimental physicist at Osaka University known for trapped-ion quantum information and laser cooling of calcium ions.

properties.name: Stephan Reitzenstein
properties.short_bio: Stephan Reitzenstein is an experimental physicist at TU Berlin working on semiconductor quantum-dot single-photon sources and nanophotonic devices.

properties.name: Steven Prawer
properties.short_bio: Steven Prawer is an experimental physicist at the University of Melbourne known for diamond-based quantum technologies and color-center engineering.

properties.name: Charles Stuart Adams
properties.short_bio: Stuart Adams is an experimental physicist at Durham University known for Rydberg-atom quantum optics, Rydberg electrometry and nonlinear optics with cold atoms.

properties.name: Thomas F. Gallagher

current_position.title: Jesse W. Beams Professor of Physics

properties.short_bio: Thomas Gallagher is an experimental physicist at the University of Virginia and a leading authority on Rydberg atoms, author of the standard monograph Rydberg Atoms.

properties.name: Tilman Pfau
properties.short_bio: Tilman Pfau is an experimental physicist at the University of Stuttgart known for dipolar quantum gases, quantum droplets and Rydberg-atom physics.

properties.name: Timothy P. Softley
properties.short_bio: Timothy Softley is a physical chemist at the University of Birmingham known for cold-molecule and ion-molecule reaction dynamics and Rydberg-molecule control.

properties.name: Tord Claeson
properties.short_bio: Tord Claeson is an experimental physicist at Chalmers known for superconductivity, Josephson junctions and superconducting quantum devices.

properties.name: Wonho Jhe
properties.short_bio: Wonho Jhe is an experimental physicist at Seoul National University working on atom optics, near-field optics and high-sensitivity nanomechanical sensing.

properties.name: Yoshihisa Yamamoto
properties.short_bio: Yoshihisa Yamamoto is a physicist at Stanford and NTT known for quantum optics, single-photon sources and the coherent Ising machine approach to optical computing.

properties.name: Mark Thompson
properties.short_bio: Mark Thompson is an experimental physicist at the University of Bristol and a pioneer of silicon integrated quantum photonics; he co-founded PsiQuantum.

properties.name: Ran Finkelstein

current_position.title: Senior Lecturer, School of Physics and Astronomy

properties.short_bio: Dr. Ran Finkelstein is an experimental physicist and Senior Lecturer in the School of Physics and Astronomy at Tel Aviv University, where he leads a laboratory on quantum information with atoms and photons. His research spans quantum computation, quantum metrology, and quantum simulation with arrays of ultracold neutral atoms held in optical tweezers, as well as quantum optics — the generation, storage, and interaction of single photons with atomic ensembles.

properties.name: Ksenia Khabarova
properties.short_bio: Ksenia Khabarova is an experimental physicist at the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) and the Russian Quantum Center in Moscow, working on trapped-ion quantum computing with ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) ions and on optical atomic clocks and precision frequency metrology. She is part of the joint FIAN–RQC group that built Russia's ion-based quantum computer using qudit (ququart) encoding.

properties.name: Nikolai Kolachevsky
properties.short_bio: Nikolai Kolachevsky is an experimental physicist and Director of the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow. He co-leads the joint FIAN–Russian Quantum Center trapped-ion programme that built Russia's ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) qudit-based quantum computer, and has a long record in optical atomic clocks and precision spectroscopy.

properties.name: Ilya Semerikov
properties.short_bio: Ilya Semerikov is an experimental physicist at the P. N. Lebedev Physical Institute (FIAN) and the Russian Quantum Center in Moscow, and a laureate of the VYZOV national prize. He led the development of Russia's ion-based quantum computer, which uses ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) ions in a linear trap with qudit (ququart) encoding and was reported at the 50-qubit scale in 2024.
